title: Trio with bass and drums, Hidden Treasures
summary: He loves playing baritone with bass and drums, recorded Hidden Treasures with Christian McBride and Billy Drummond, and plays tunes to reach audiences.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Critics, polls and the jazz press

blocks.x: In some time. I read a small thing about — that you enjoy playing with just drums and bass. © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -16-

I do. I love playing — that’s my chosen environment. I had the great pleasure of recording with Christian McBride and Billy Drummond and we did a trio record called “Hidden Treasures.” And the freedom in that, without a piano or without a guitar is, for me, just magic. Because I just feel free to kind of go and take the music in any direction, where I can kind of go where I want without being kind of locked in with chords. And that’s hard work too, because it’s hard to stop, it’s like kind of you have to play all night. But that’s okay, I really like that. Ideally that’s the group that I would like to go out and play with. But it’s challenging for the audience. I think it’s hard to get club owners to book that, because first of all to get a baritone sax player booked at all it’s kind of hard to get past that, and then, without a piano, that’s kind of tricky.
Yeah. I suppose you’re asking quite a bit from your audience.

It’s demanding. But I try to play tunes, or tunes based on standards, you know, so I try to not make it too alienating and try to bring them in in terms of playing tunes or playing material that kind of brings them in. Because the bottom line at the end of the day is that people are coming to hear us play and we’re trying to play something that makes them feel good. Right? And to reach them in some way. So even though you’re playing with just bass and drums I think you can still do that.
